prose_updates.tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but published AWRI rule selection relies on simulation. Conditioning on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set and applying a three-state forest recursion with \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion yields an exact, fully evaluated dense algorithm for every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law in \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bit operations. The tagged laws reconstruct every dense RDIM risk matrix. Rational weak semidefinite optimization then returns an independently checkable \(\varepsilon\)-minimax certificate in time polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\); for canonical \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\), this dependence is polynomial in \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\). When the supplied core is a vertex cover, an entered-subset cumulative-exponent dynamic program evaluates every admissible chamber implicitly and computes all tagged laws, with no unevaluated integral, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. An evaluated recurrence also covers identical replicated-star attachments, but fixed-parameter closure for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains open.

project_justification.gap: AWRI fixes the weighted greedy design and balanced RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate. Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, while structural graph programs count static sets. General semidefinite design methods neither supply the exact WRI/RDIM risk matrices nor give an end-to-end rational certificate with complexity measured against the binary encoding of an arbitrary rational tolerance. None of these results gives the evaluated heterogeneous tagged integration used here. The entered-subset dynamic program closes the vertex-cover special case, without an integration gate, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations, but arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments still lack a fixed-parameter representation.
project_justification.niche: A supplied feedback set exposes a forest decomposition on which exact heterogeneous priority integration is possible. The proved general guarantee is XP in the feedback size. If the supplied core is a vertex cover, every exterior component is a singleton and the cumulative priority exponent is determined by the subset of core coordinates already entered; this yields an \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) dynamic program with polynomial rational height. Identical attachment profiles give a second evaluated special regime. Once the exact rational risk library is available, the finite ellipsoidal risk game admits a rational primal-dual certificate whose computation is polynomial in the encoded tolerance; for dyadic tolerance \(2^{-p}\), it is polynomial in \(p\).
project_justification.fill: The paper proves core inclusion--exclusion, a fully evaluated dense chamber-polynomial algorithm with controlled rational bit height, exact tagged RDIM risk reconstruction, and a rational near-minimax certificate. In the vertex-cover subclass, it replaces factorial chamber enumeration by an entered-subset recurrence, obtaining all tagged laws exactly and without unevaluated integrals in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations with polynomial intermediate rational height. The certificate algorithm is polynomial in \(L\), \(n\), \(\Lambda\), and the binary encoding length of \(\varepsilon\), specializing to polynomial dependence on \(p=\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\) for canonical dyadic input \(\varepsilon=2^{-p}\). The paper records arbitrary-forest fixed-parameter moment closure as an open problem rather than assuming it.

prose_updates.related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li supply the published directed-network FNI/TTE/WRI plus balanced-RDIM causal-design construction used here. This note first identifies WRI deletion with greedy maximal-independent-set selection on the neighborhood-overlap conflict graph, and then proves exact algorithms only for the positive-integer-weight subclass with a supplied feedback set. Positive rational priority weights transfer by multiplying all exponential, equivalently Beta, rates by a common denominator, which preserves their random order; arbitrary published real weights are not covered by the exact Turing-model algorithms. Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li derive a balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate and use simulation for candidate-weight selection. Pippenger's random-sequential-adsorption recursions, Gamarnik and Goldberg's rooted-tree bonus recursions, and the local-limit equations of Krivelevich, Meszaros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman do not compute exact finite heterogeneous tagged moments. Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li count static independent sets on bounded-treewidth graphs, and Borie, Parker, and Tovey give finite-state decomposition methods, but neither weights maximal independent sets by heterogeneous priority orders. Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk establish a \(2^{O(k\log k)}\) scale for a different feedback-set problem, not an oracle for the present integration. The present \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) vertex-cover bound instead comes from a problem-specific entered-subset dynamic program for cumulative cutoff exponents; it contains no unevaluated integral and does not settle heterogeneous forest closure. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje study an unrestricted network-experiment minimax functional; no equality with that functional is claimed. Kallus motivates mixed minimax design, and Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong develop semidefinite minimax-design methods. Boyd and Vandenberghe supply the finite-dimensional separating-hyperplane theorem and its open-set converse used in the minimax interchange. Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver's Theorem 4.3.13 supplies weak constrained convex minimization for centered convex bodies given by weak-membership and convex-function value oracles; the rational affine-SDP parametrization, radius bounds, membership tests, and pullback needed here are proved separately in this note. Aronow and Samii provide the design-based interference framework. Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet motivate the rural-China insurance application but provide no evidence that its measured conflict graph has small feedback number or a small vertex cover.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact algorithm removes Monte Carlo error from comparison of prespecified WRI rules, but its worst-case general cost is XP rather than fixed-parameter in the feedback number. If a measured conflict graph comes with a small vertex-cover core, the entered-subset cumulative-exponent program gives exact tagged-law computation, with no integration gate, in \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) bit operations and with polynomial intermediate rational bit length. Identical repeated attachments admit a separate evaluated recurrence. Neither special case establishes fixed-parameter tractability for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments. The final semidefinite certificate concerns worst-case squared error of the fixed RDIM rule library over the stated endpoint ellipsoid; it is not a claim of optimality among all network designs or estimators.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The dense chamber-polynomial representation closes arbitrary heterogeneous branching, component products, moving endpoints, and tags, but uses \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) states. It therefore proves an evaluated XP theorem, not the originally proposed fixed-parameter theorem. In the vertex-cover case, every exterior component is a singleton, so the entered core subset \(S\subseteq\mathcal K\) determines the scalar cumulative exponent \(E_{\mathcal U,\mathcal B}(S)\); this is exactly why the \(2^k\)-state recurrence closes. Branching forest components instead retain distinct future ordered-ratio exponent profiles. Two heterogeneous branches can have the same present activation count and exponent while leaving different exponents on future variables. The unresolved question is whether a shared operator representation can preserve those profiles in \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) time. A table indexed by \(k\) degree totals, a profile-count vector with an \(n\)-dependent exponent, or a circuit retaining an integration gate does not solve that question.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The general proved result assumes a supplied feedback set, positive integer priority weights, and permits XP dependence \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\); it neither finds a minimum feedback set nor proves arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability. The exact \(L6^k\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) guarantee, absence of an unevaluated integral, and polynomial rational height require that the supplied feedback core also be a vertex cover; the other evaluated special result concerns the stated identical replicated-star coefficient. Nondegenerate isolation is required only for RDIM denominators and risk reconstruction. The minimax result chooses within a prespecified WRI/RDIM library over a graph-Sobolev endpoint ellipsoid and does not equal the unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional. The rural-China follow-up is a prospective consumer, not evidence for a small empirical feedback number, a small vertex cover, a calibrated ellipsoid, or improved field performance.
